summary: Heike Oberlin is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen (MA 1990–1999, Habilitation by 2013), Kerala Kalamandalam, and the University of Würzburg (PhD 2004). She held posts at Tübingen (2005–2008), Kalamandalam (2018), and Rome (2025).

Heiner Eichner was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg under Karl Hoffmann (~1966–1974) and served as a professor at the University of Vienna (~1989–2010).
Heinrich August Jäschke was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He served as co-director at Pädagogium Niesky in 1847 and worked as a missionary for the Moravian Church from 1857 to 1868.

Heinrich Blochmann specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig under Fleischer, Paris under Hase, and Calcutta. He held posts at Fort William College, Doveton College, and Aliah University (principal 1865, 1870).
Heinrich Brunn was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Bonn (~1839–1843). He later served on the faculty at the University of Munich (~1865–1894).

Heinrich Ewald was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen under Eichhorn, Tychsen, and the Plancks (PhD 1823). He held professorships at the University of Göttingen (1824–1837, 1848–1867) and the University of Tübingen (1838–1848).

Heinrich Hettrich worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Saarland University and Giessen, and completing his Habilitation at Munich (1984). He held posts at Saarland, Salzburg, Zurich, Marburg (~1988–1989), and the University of Würzburg as chair holder from 1989.

Heinrich Hübschmann worked in linguistics, Iranian studies, and Indology. He studied at Jena, Tübingen, Munich (PhD under Martin Haug), and Leipzig. He was an associate professor at Leipzig University (1876) and professor of comparative linguistics at Strasbourg from 1877.

Heinrich Kiepert was a geographer and historian who studied at Berlin under Boeckh and Petermann, earning his doctorate at Jena (~1842–1843). He led the geographical department at Landes-Industrie-Comptoir and became a professor of geography at Berlin in 1874.

Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy and Chézy, later holding the chair of Oriental languages at Leipzig University from 1836.

Heinrich Lenz studied at the Imperial University of Dorpat (~1820–1823). He held academic posts at Saint Peter's School, the Main Pedagogical Institute, the Mikhailovsky Artillery School, and Saint Petersburg State University (1836–1865).

Heinrich Lüders was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held posts at Oxford, Göttingen, Rostock, and Kiel, before serving as chair of ancient Indian language and literature at Berlin (1909–1935).

Heinrich Rickert was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1884–1885) and the University of Strasbourg (~1886–1888). He later held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1891–1916) and Heidelberg University (~1916–1932).
Heinrich Rückert was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1845–1852) and the University of Breslau (~1852–1875).
Heinrich Schliemann was a scholar of history and archaeology. He pursued studies at the University of Paris from 1866 to 1868 and at the University of Rostock in ~1869.

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Zurich under Hirzel, Orelli, and Sauppe, later serving there as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics (1841–1889), alongside teaching at Kantonsschule Rämibühl and Höhere Töchterschule Zürich.

Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University under Hermann Brockhaus, earning his Dr. phil. (~1865–1877). He served as a teacher of classical languages at the Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.

Heinrich Wenzel was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He studied at Jena, Tübingen (PhD), and Leipzig, with instruction from Jäschke, Feer, Müller, and Gabelentz, completing his Habilitation at Leipzig University in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Tübingen, Strasbourg, and Berlin under Roth, Goldschmidt, Weber, Scherer, and Windisch. He held posts at Berlin, Greifswald (professor from 1881), Heidelberg, and Columbia University.

Heinrich von Stietencron was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Munich, SOAS London, and Heidelberg (Habilitation), where he assisted Hermann Berger. He later served as chair holder at the University of Tübingen from 1973 to 1998.
